title: How it was sold, and how its successor was announced
lede: Eight videos, all still on the YouTube channels of the companies involved or of the press. Years are the upload dates shown by YouTube; we have not confirmed where else the spots ran.

videos.title: Criterion: “Introducing FilmStruck”
videos.caption: A three-minute introduction on the Criterion Collection’s channel, uploaded on October 6, 2016, the day the prices and the first launch date were announced.[^41][^4]

videos.title: TCM: “Introducing FilmStruck: Free Trial”
videos.caption: A 31-second spot on Turner Classic Movies’ channel, uploaded on October 13, 2016, six days before the original launch date. The service offered a 14-day free trial when it opened on November 1.[^41][^7]

videos.title: Criterion: “Adventures in Moviegoing: Bill Hader’s First Date”
videos.caption: A 52-second excerpt from the Criterion Channel’s guest-programmer series, uploaded on November 10, 2016. Hader later signed the first letter to Warner Bros.[^41][^26]

videos.title: TechCrunch: “FilmStruck Can Provide Your Art Movie Fix”
videos.caption: A short news item on TechCrunch’s channel, uploaded on November 18, 2016. TechCrunch’s written report of the launch is one of our sources.[^41][^8]

videos.title: FilmStruck UK: “Welcome to FilmStruck!”
videos.caption: A one-minute spot on the British service’s own channel, uploaded on February 7, 2018, the month FilmStruck Curzon opened.[^41][^11]

videos.title: TCM: “TCM Select now on FilmStruck”
videos.caption: Uploaded by Turner Classic Movies on February 26, 2018, the day the Warner Bros. classics deal was announced.[^41][^12]

videos.title: Criterion: “New, Independent Criterion Channel to Launch Spring 2019”
videos.caption: Criterion’s video announcement of its independent service, uploaded on November 20, 2018, nine days before FilmStruck’s last day.[^41][^29]

videos.title: Criterion: “Criterion Channel Trailer”
videos.caption: The trailer for the relaunched channel, uploaded on March 22, 2019, ahead of the April 8 opening.[^41][^35]

note: We describe each video by its title, uploader, length and upload date as YouTube shows them. FilmStruck’s own U.S. channel still carries a 31-second “Introducing FilmStruck” that we have not embedded because it appears to duplicate the TCM spot.
